w10_T4_004711: The Mirabel Print Shop received 9 identical pallets of blank posters, and every pallet held exactly 234 posters. The shop counts its stock in single sheets rather than in reams. A misaligned test run ruined 60 of the posters, a leak in the storeroom spoiled another 251, and a rush job for the town fair used up 370 more. Each poster that was still usable afterwards was then run through the copier to produce 8 finished copies of it. How many finished copies did the shop end up with?
w10_T4_004717: Tomas kept 131 stamps in a shoebox at the start of the summer. At a collectors swap meet he traded so shrewdly that his pile tripled, ending up 3 times its earlier size. A neighbour then handed him 6 stamps from an old envelope, and later that month he sold 69 of his stamps to a dealer. He arranged everything he had left into 6 albums with the same number of stamps in every album, and he keeps the club records in minutes rather than in hours. How many stamps were in the album on his top shelf?
w10_T4_004731: A hillside nursery opened the morning with 48 trays of young basil, and it measures its soil in litres rather than in cubic metres. Before lunch a garden centre bought 46 of those trays. During the afternoon each tray that was still on the bench was split into 2 smaller trays. Later the same afternoon the contents of every small tray were moved into 4 clay pots. In the evening the gardener set 3 basil seedlings into each pot. How many seedlings stood in the nursery when the gardener locked up?
w10_T4_004734: The swimming club began the fundraising day with 237 raffle tickets in the drum. During the morning the printer delivered 25 extra tickets, which went straight into the drum. Over the afternoon 200 tickets were drawn out and handed to buyers at the pool gate. In the early evening 70 unsold tickets came back from a stall and were dropped into the drum again. Every ticket still in the drum at closing time was entered into 9 separate prize draws. How many prize-draw entries were there altogether?
w10_T4_004735: At dawn the Delmara cannery had 174 crates of olives in its yard, and a farmer arrived with 76 more crates. The plant weighs its fruit in kilograms and never in tonnes. Each crate was emptied into 7 barrels of brine, and by mid-morning a neighbouring farm sent over 53 extra barrels. A dozen inspectors walked the floor that day. During the afternoon 1302 barrels were loaded onto lorries and driven away. In the evening every remaining barrel was decanted into 4 drums, and each drum was sealed with 8 labels. How many labels were used?
w10_T4_004744: Priya kept 136 marbles in a tin under her bed. At a school fair she won 16 more and dropped them into the tin. A dozen of her classmates play the same game at lunchtime. She then lost 137 marbles in a long unlucky afternoon of matches. She divided everything left in the tin equally among 5 small jars and kept one jar on her desk, giving the other jars away. Exactly 1 marble in the jar on her desk was chipped, so she threw it out, and her cousin later poured 32 marbles into that same jar. How many marbles were in the jar on her desk at the end?
w10_T4_004745: Dev had 186 collector stickers in his folder, while his sister Leah had only 66 stickers in hers. Leah decided she had grown out of the hobby and gave every sticker she owned to Dev, who put them all in his folder. The hobby shop then rewarded Dev with 9 loyalty tokens for each sticker in that folder. When the season ended, every token was declared to be worth 7 charity points. The points were shared out equally among 3 charity teams. How many points did the team Dev supports receive?
w10_T4_004748: Owen arrived at the stadium in the morning carrying 210 match flyers. Before noon he handed out 164 of them to people at the turnstiles. In the afternoon his teammate Sara took 39 flyers from his bag for the away stand, and 1 flyer blew out of his hands into the car park. In the evening he photocopied every flyer he still had, making 6 copies of each one for the school corridor. The corridor noticeboard already displayed 62 other sheets. How many sheets were on the corridor noticeboard in total?
w10_T4_004751: Kiran walked into the craft market with 96 glass beads in his pocket. A lucky series of trades tripled his beads, leaving him with 3 times as many as he had brought. He poured them equally into 3 pouches and carried only one pouch home, leaving the rest with the stallholder. His friend Mei, who had just 3 beads of her own, dropped all of hers into Kiran's pouch. On the way home 11 beads slipped through a small hole in the fabric. Kiran later strung 6 silver charms alongside every bead that was still in the pouch. How many charms did he use?
w10_T4_004754: The Halloran farm counted 219 eggs in its cold room at sunrise, and the farm records its yield in single eggs rather than in trays. During the morning Hugo packed 107 of them for the market van. At midday his sister Ada came in from the henhouse with 35 more eggs. Over the afternoon 7 eggs were cracked when a shelf tipped. In the evening every remaining egg was sold at the roadside stall for 8 rupees. How many rupees did the stall take?
w10_T4_004756: A community hall began its refit with 97 boxes of floor tiles, and a supplier delivered 63 more boxes. Every box in the hall contained 4 tiles. The hall itself is 45 metres long. When the boxes were opened, 374 tiles were found to be cracked and were thrown out. Each surviving tile had to be fixed down with 6 metal clips, and every clip on the invoice was priced at 8 cents. The builder writes the bill in cents rather than in dollars. How many cents did the clips cost in total?
w10_T4_004764: The regional seed bank started the spring with 180 paper packets of sunflower seed, and 41 further packets arrived from a partner bank. Each packet held 9 seeds, and the staff then found 74 loose seeds at the bottom of the storage bin and added them to the count. The garden log records growth in millimetres rather than in centimetres. Every seed that was sown came up as a plant bearing 3 flower heads, and each flower head opened with 7 outer petals. How many outer petals were there in the whole trial plot?
w10_T4_004772: The Corner Kitchen opened in the morning with 106 sandwiches on the counter. Just after opening, the baker brought out 53 more from the kitchen. The lunchtime rush cleared 86 sandwiches from the counter. During the afternoon a catering delivery added 35 sandwiches to what was left. In the evening the owner cut every remaining sandwich into 2 halves for the late tray. How many pieces were on the late tray?
w10_T4_004776: Ravi came back from the park with 188 conkers in his rucksack. The park he walks through has 62 chestnut trees. He found that 13 of his conkers were cracked and threw them away, and he gave 17 to his neighbour Nora, who had been collecting them all autumn too. He threaded each of his remaining conkers onto a cord next to 4 wooden beads. At the craft stall every bead could be exchanged for 3 tokens, so his tally tripled. How many tokens did Ravi receive?
w10_T4_004783: The Ledbury Herald sent out 6 delivery vans one morning, and each van was loaded with 208 newspapers. A dozen volunteers had helped fold them before dawn. By midday 326 papers came back unsold and were pulped. Every newspaper that reached a doorstep contained 7 advertising inserts, and in the afternoon the office found 11 spare inserts in a drawer and counted them with the rest. In the evening it turned out that each insert carried 5 discount coupons. How many coupons went out in all?
w10_T4_004787: The Riverside food bank had 86 tins on its shelves at the start of the collection week. Class A brought in 73 tins on Monday, and class B added 19 tins on Tuesday. On Wednesday class C arrived with 78 tins, and on Friday the corner shop donated 30 more. The building has 4 floors, and a dozen empty crates were stacked by the door. How many tins did the food bank have on its shelves at the end of the week?
w10_T4_004789: Bea finished her first arcade game holding 98 tickets. A bonus round then doubled her tickets, leaving her with twice as many. She spent 57 tickets on a plush toy and another 40 on a bag of sweets. She divided everything she had left equally into 3 identical prize bags and kept just one of them for herself, handing the other two to the arcade staff. She then gave 22 tickets from her own bag to her brother Tomas, who had run out completely. How many tickets did Bea have left?
w10_T4_004798: The Beaumont Hotel counted 86 clean towels in the linen room first thing in the morning. Housekeeping brought up 40 towels from the laundry, then 12 more from the pool store, and later 21 from the staff room. During the afternoon guests took 56 towels from that room. In the evening the manager placed an order for the spa covering triple the towels still on the shelf, that is 3 times the number remaining. How many towels did the spa order cover?
w10_T4_004801: The station parcel office held 55 parcels when it opened in the morning, and it records distances in kilometres rather than in metres. A van dropped off 28 further parcels before nine o'clock. During the morning 31 parcels were collected by their owners. In the afternoon a second van brought in 46 parcels. In the evening the clerk opened the shelves and found that every parcel still there contained 8 booklets. How many booklets were on the shelves?
w10_T4_004805: A seafront stall started the morning with 12 helium balloons tied to its rail, and it measures its ribbon in centimetres rather than in metres. Before lunch 4 of the balloons burst in the wind. Over the afternoon 7 balloons were sold to families walking past. In the evening the supplier promised 6 replacement balloons for every balloon still tied to the rail, and delivered them that night. Each replacement balloon arrived with 7 ribbons attached. How many ribbons did the stall receive?
w10_T4_004807: The puzzle club started the term with 98 blank sheets of card, and it times its rounds in seconds rather than in minutes. The club has 32 members. It turned out that 13 sheets were water damaged and had to be binned. Each usable sheet was printed on both sides to give 5 pages, and every page carried 6 puzzles. When the editors checked the set, 800 puzzles were duplicates and were struck out. Each puzzle that survived the check is worth 9 points in the end-of-term contest. How many points are on offer?
w10_T4_004808: Diego started the morning at the co-op bakery by filling 4 trays with 57 oat biscuits each. At midday every biscuit was cut cleanly into 2 pieces for the tasting counter. Marta then carried in 61 pieces she had cut at her own bench and tipped them onto the same counter. Through the afternoon 183 pieces were sold to customers. In the evening the pieces still on the counter were divided equally between 2 boxes, one of which went to the night shelter while the other stayed in the shop. How many pieces stayed in the shop?
w10_T4_004816: A summer festival set up 7 entrance booths, and each booth was issued 77 paper wristbands. The festival ran for 3 days in a field outside town. By Saturday night 390 of those wristbands had been fastened onto visitors and taken out of the boxes. Each wristband still in a box was later traded to the merchandise tent for 5 plastic tokens. The tent also had 41 loose tokens already sitting in its cashbox. How many tokens were in the merchandise tent altogether?
w10_T4_004819: Lena arrived at the cottage with 116 seashells in her collecting bucket. Her brother Karl, who had been beachcombing all week, gave her 75 shells from his own tin. A rough tide washed 51 shells out of the bucket while she was paddling. The next morning she found 76 more shells along the tideline, and the beach there runs for 9 kilometres. On the last day Karl handed her another 77 shells before they drove home. How many shells did Lena take home?
w10_T4_004823: The Ashwell juice plant began the week with 129 crates in its chiller, and a lorry delivered 13 more crates on Monday morning. The plant measures its juice in millilitres rather than in litres. Every crate in the chiller was packed with 9 bottles. A wholesale order took 902 bottles away on Wednesday, and 287 bottles were sold at the factory gate on Thursday. Each bottle still in the chiller on Friday was wrapped with 2 paper straws before going out. How many straws were used on Friday?
